title: Latency cresting and request unfairness after autoscale burst — incident review and remediation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During an autoscale burst in the EU-GPU pool we observed a coordinated rise in 95th/99th percentile generation latency and a distinct unfairness pattern where priority=low requests experienced near-total batch starvation for 18 minutes. The event coincided with a scheduled capacity expansion triggered by a synthetic traffic surge test from a partner. Rough numbers: 2.1M requests affected, median latency unchanged (~45ms) but p95 rose from 120ms to 2.4s and p99 rose to 6.8s. Two paying customers reported user-facing slowdowns; internal SLOs for latency were breached.

root_cause: A combination of autoscale-triggered worker churn and a regression in the priority-aware coalescer heuristic. New workers were added and started with empty KV caches and default coalescer timers. The coalescer heuristics attempted aggressive latency targets for high-priority traffic, which starved lower-priority lanes when coalescer windows on new nodes misaligned with the coordinator. A recent change (runtime-1.24) to the coalescer timer reset logic caused newly provisioned workers to report zero available slots to the slot allocator for short durations, amplifying batch formation stalls.
mitigations_taken: Routed a fraction of traffic to stable legacy pool (eu-legacy) to offload pressure from new workers
Reduced coalescer max window on new nodes from 40ms to 12ms to prioritize forming smaller, fair batches
Enabled temporary priority relaxation: allow low-priority requests to preempt idle slots after 10ms
Rolled a hotfix (runtime PR #4721) that prevents zero-slot registration during worker initialization
Added ad-hoc KV cache warmup by replaying recent prefix traces for new nodes
postmortem_findings: Worker initialization path can report transient zero-slots leading to slot allocator starvation
Coalescer timer reset combined with coordinator slot sampling created phase alignment where many nodes refused low-priority load
Autoscale event exposed the delta between per-node heuristics and global coordinator expectations
No automated canary validated fairness metrics during autoscale operations; our canary only tracked median latency
Runbook lacked a rapid knob to temporarily relax priority enforcement cluster-wide

acceptance_criteria: New workers never report zero available slots for >250ms during normal init (verified by telemetry)
Autoscale canary shows no p99 regressions for low-priority lanes in staged deployments
Emergency priority-relax toggle exists and is tested end-to-end in the runbook
Latency and fairness dashboards updated with per-priority histograms and retrospectives added to Console
notes: This incident surfaced a class of failure that only appears when node churn is both high and synchronized with tight coalescer windows. Long-term we should consider decoupling local heuristic reset from global slot allocation by introducing a short grace registration period for new nodes. We will run a focused chaos test in the next cycle that simulates rapid node joins under varied priority mixes.
